rpy-parity-d1f65c8c0.text: `python/cpp/bindings_proportion.cpp::fast_zero_one_inflated_beta` (return_mismatch): The Python binding returns only params, neg_loglik, num_iter, hit_iteration_cap, converged and gradient_norm (bindings_proportion.cpp:130-137). It drops b, log_phi, zero_one_b0 and zero_one_b1, and also vcov, observed_information, fisher_information, information, hessian and min_eigenvalue_information. The R export returns all of these. It has no estimate_only argument, although R documents 'estimate_only: If TRUE, skip the post-fit Hessian/variance computation'. The docstring never says that no variance matrix is returned, and it lists no return fields at all. Suggested: Either return vcov, the information matrices and the split coefficient blocks from the binding (the vcov code at R/EDI/src/fast_zero_one_inflated_beta.cpp:630-666 would need to move into a shared internal function), or add a docstring sentence saying the binding returns only the listed fields and no vcov or information. A human should choose which.

rpy-parity-d62675f61.text: `python/cpp/bindings_glmm.cpp::fast_clogit_plus_glmm` (argument_mismatch): The R export has weights_disc and weights_conc, and the R class passes them: weights_disc = disc_weights, weights_conc = conc_weights. The Python binding has no counterpart and hard-codes std::nullopt, std::nullopt for both when it calls the kernel (bindings_glmm.cpp:453). These weights change the fitted likelihood, so Python cannot reproduce R fits that use them. The docstring does not mention that the weights are unsupported. Suggested: Add optional weights_disc and weights_conc arguments to the binding and pass them to fast_clogit_plus_glmm_internal. Otherwise, document that observation weights are not exposed.
